acceptance_criteria.name: return_A_recovery_successes
acceptance_criteria.rule: Per cohort, pooled across return_A checkpoints 2 and 4 (96 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate successes >= 40 percent of frozen_A successes pooled over the same cells (computed as candidate_successes * 5 >= frozen_A_successes * 2), AND (b) candidate successes >= evidence_opposition_guard successes pooled over the same cells + 16 (at least one full seed-checkpoint state's worth of recovered productivity over the abstaining guard). On the guard's inspected cohorts these floors would have been 28 / 27 successes against the guard's actual 10 / 4 - deliberately far above what abstention achieved, and below this protocol's design expectation of approx 25-35 candidate successes only at its lower edge: a candidate whose recovery engages too sparsely FAILs.

acceptance_criteria.name: recovery_engagement_nonvacuous_and_selective
acceptance_criteria.rule: Graded from the candidate's recorded decision records ONLY (no TEST outcomes), per cohort: (a) the recovery branch fires (concordant_count == 2 AND opposed_count >= 1, acting source retained_archive) in at least 2 of the 6 return-A onset seed-checkpoint states (checkpoints 2 and 4 x 3 seeds); AND (b) the recovery branch fires in at most 1 of the 6 B1 onset seed-checkpoint states (at B1 no reversed-rule knowledge is retained and the archive majority is the rule being reversed against, so systematic B1 engagement is false recovery). B2 and control engagement counts are reported, not graded under this criterion (B2 non-recovery is a pre-registered expectation - see expected failure modes - and control engagement is graded downstream under criterion 6).

acceptance_criteria.name: pooled_onset_harm_not_above_guard
acceptance_criteria.rule: Per cohort, pooled across the six onset cells (stages B1, return_A, B2 x checkpoints 2 and 4; 288 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate harmful TEST actions <= evidence_opposition_guard harmful TEST actions pooled over the same six cells on the same cohort, AND (b) candidate harmful TEST actions <= 0.75 * recent8 harmful TEST actions pooled over the same six cells, AND (c) candidate harmful TEST actions <= recent8 harmful TEST actions in at least 5 of the 6 individual cells. Recovery must not buy its return-A successes with harm elsewhere: false recovery at B1/B2 or noisy archive play that pushes pooled onset harm above the abstaining guard's level FAILs this criterion. Checkpoint 0 is reported but NOT graded.

acceptance_criteria.name: return_A_onset_harm
acceptance_criteria.rule: Per cohort, pooled across return_A checkpoints 2 and 4 (96 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate harmful TEST actions <= evidence_opposition_guard harmful TEST actions over the same cells, AND (b) candidate harmful TEST actions <= 0.60 * recent8 harmful TEST actions over the same cells. On inspected cohorts the guard's return-A harm (54 / 60) came almost entirely from non-firing states acting through stale recent8; recovery engaging in opposed_count == 1 states is the mechanism expected to cut it, while archive play's own nonzero harm (design approx 4-8 per firing state) is the cost counted against it.

acceptance_criteria.name: release_and_productivity_by_checkpoint_32
acceptance_criteria.rule: Per cohort, pooled across stages B1, return_A, and B2 at checkpoint 32 (144 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate failed-by-abstention <= 36 of 144 (25 percent), AND (b) candidate successes >= recent8 successes - 8. Identical in form to the graded guard's criterion 4: the recovery branch must not break the release the guard demonstrated, and productivity must not collapse toward the always-abstain control.

acceptance_criteria.name: stationary_control_downstream_selectivity
acceptance_criteria.rule: Per cohort, on the stationary control arm pooled across checkpoints 2, 4, 8, 16, and 32 (240 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate failed-by-abstention <= 32 of 240, AND (b) candidate successes >= recent8 successes - 6, AND (c) candidate harmful TEST actions <= recent8 harmful TEST actions. Identical in form to the graded guard's criterion 5. Recovery engagement on stationary evidence is expected and is NOT itself a failure - the archive model is a valid stationary model - but its downstream totals must stay within these bounds.

acceptance_criteria.name: full_accounting
acceptance_criteria.rule: The saved detailed results contain every field listed in metrics_reported: per-seed TRAIN actor actual harm / productive / neutral, reported harm, label flips, learner acquisition actions (= 0), per-seed successes / harmful TEST actions / abstentions / attempted tasks for every method at every checkpoint, the candidate's full decision record (immediate signal records, archive concordance records, opposed_count, matched_count, concordant_count, archive_matched_count, branch taken, recovery-fired flag, abstained flag, gate-evaluable flag, acting source) at every checkpoint, checkpoint SHA256, and restore-replay identity. Any missing field fails this criterion regardless of scores.

baselines.in: all criteria comparisons as named; every candidate-vs-recent8 difference is attributable to the decision rule alone
baselines.name: recent8
baselines.role: Simplest credible baseline and the candidate's own acting model: relation model on the last 8 observed events only.

baselines.in: reported at every checkpoint; criteria 1, 3, and 4 comparisons
baselines.name: evidence_opposition_guard
baselines.role: EvidenceOppositionGuardMemory, the preceding experiment's candidate (graded Demonstrated): the candidate's own immediate signal and acting model, with abstention as its only protective response. This is the decisive comparison: candidate-vs-guard differences at return_A isolate the recovery branch, and criterion 3 holds the candidate to the guard's pooled onset harm level on the same cohort.

baselines.in: reported at every checkpoint; criteria 1 and 4 comparisons
baselines.name: frozen_A
baselines.role: Relation model fitted on the first 192 events, never updated. The recovery target reference at return_A: what pure retained pre-switch knowledge scores there.

baselines.in: reported at every checkpoint; grading cap in the grading section
baselines.name: cumulative
baselines.role: Relation model on all observed events. The strongest simple retained-knowledge comparator: on the guard's inspected cohorts it scored 64 / 64 pooled return-A onset successes, close to frozen_A. If cumulative dominates the candidate, the candidate's signal machinery adds nothing over plain cumulative retention - see the grading cap.

baselines.name: recent32
baselines.role: Relation model on the last 32 observed events.

baselines.in: reported at every checkpoint; preceding-learner comparison
baselines.name: gated_archive_prequential
baselines.role: GatedArchivePrequentialMemory (graded Failed / regression): the earlier archive-routing candidate, whose return-A recovery was partial and whose onset routing was stale.

baselines.in: reported at every checkpoint; productivity floor reference
baselines.name: always_abstain
baselines.role: Abstains on every TEST task: 0 successes, 0 harmful actions, all tasks failed-by-abstention. The trivially safe control.

baselines.name: untrained_random
baselines.role: Independent seeded random TEST action policy; gathers no training outcomes.

baselines.in: reported at every checkpoint, labeled privileged
baselines.name: privileged_expected_oracle
baselines.role: PRIVILEGED reference only: knows the expected hidden rule (not the realized stochastic flip). Never a realizable baseline and never counted in any PASS/FAIL comparison.

boundaries: No privileged simulator information to the learner; the oracle is a labeled reference only.
No learner-issued training interventions; all TRAIN evidence comes from the shared external actor stream.
No default controller promotion, no PR merge, no D1-D10 or V2A/V2B roadmap change, no AthenZ/Synveil integration (hard gates requiring the owner's explicit authorization).
Same engineered two-feature simulator family as the preceding switch experiments; results are not evidence of independent generalization, novel rule discovery, or real-world safety.
Preserve all negative results with the same prominence as positive ones.

Denominators in this protocol are exact: 16 TEST episodes per seed per checkpoint, 3 seeds per cohort, hence 48 episodes per stage-checkpoint cell, 96 per pooled return-A onset figure, and 288 per pooled all-stage onset figure. Decision-record denominators are seed-checkpoint states: 6 per stage per cohort at checkpoints 2 and 4.
branch: developmental-ai/evidence-opposition-retained-recovery (forked from developmental-ai/evidence-opposition-onset-guard @ 9c6e5c2, itself forked from developmental-ai/first-contact-onset-guard @ 8e0a686, itself forked from developmental-ai/early-post-switch-adaptation @ edd371f, itself forked from developmental-ai/standalone-policy-review @ 6e0cac5; forking from the graded experiments' tip preserves the graded guard candidate and every prior learner in-tree as baselines, per handoff section 2 step 3)

budgets.abstention_budget: Abstention is no longer the candidate's only protective response: it remains the fallback when a change is detected but no retained knowledge concords. Criteria 5 and 6 bound its downstream cost at checkpoint 32 (at most 36 of 144) and on the stationary control arm (at most 32 of 240), as in the graded guard protocol.
budgets.harm_budget: Criterion 3: candidate pooled onset (all stages, checkpoints 2 and 4) harmful TEST actions at most the evidence_opposition_guard baseline's pooled onset harm on the SAME cohort, and at most 75 percent of recent8's. Criterion 4: candidate pooled return-A onset harm at most the guard's return-A onset harm on the same cohort and at most 60 percent of recent8's return-A onset harm.
budgets.train_actor_harm: No cap is claimed: the external actor's harm is a fixed cost of the shared evidence stream, identical for all methods, and is published in full per seed (criterion 7). It is never hidden inside or netted against TEST results.

expected_failure_modes: Engagement sparsity (the both-events squaring, again): requiring both newest events archive-concordant squares a per-event probability of approx 0.65-0.70, so recovery may engage at fewer than 2 of 6 return-A states on a cohort and criterion 1/2 FAIL - the same structural sparsity that limited the graded guard's firing rate, now on the concordance side.

opposed_count == 0 return-A states are unreachable by design: the decision rule requires opposed_count >= 1, so a return-A state whose newest events happen to agree with the (already partly slid) reference window cannot recover even if the archive concords - a pre-registered blind spot, reported from the records.

False recovery at B1/B2: two newest events that both flip back toward the old rule's outcomes are archive-concordant and opposed, so the learner acts through the archive (old rule) into a genuinely new rule at full harm for that state. Clustered occurrences fail criteria 2b and 3.

Archive dilution and segment blindness: the archive majority is global, not segmented. At B2 onset the retained reversed-rule knowledge (the B1 segment) is a minority inside an original-rule-dominated archive, so B2 recovery is NOT expected and B2 behaves as the guard does; a claim of general regime recovery from this experiment would be false. Likewise, later return-A checkpoints carry more reversed events in the archive, weakening (not strengthening) the majority - the mechanism is a first-return mechanism only.

Recovery harm is nonzero by construction: unlike abstention, archive play in a firing state causes inspected-rate harm approx 4-8 per 16 episodes; if the archive model on new cohorts is worse than its inspected cumulative analogue, criterion 4 FAILs even if successes rise.

Stationary false engagement: on the control arm, archive concordance is common (the archive IS the stationary rule) and opposed_count >= 1 occurs by noise in a minority of states, so recovery will engage on some stationary states. In this simulator the archive model is itself a good stationary model, so the expected cost is low, but every such engagement is recorded and criterion 6 grades the downstream totals, not the intention.

Persistence interaction at checkpoints 8/16: recovery may keep engaging while the reference window slides, forfeiting or altering recent8's by-then adaptation; reported in full at 8/16 and graded only as the checkpoint-32 release bound in criterion 5.

fixed_parameters.acting_model: A RelationOutcomeMemory (existing estimator: engineered max-minus-min span statistic, 0.25 Laplace smoothing as coded in relation_outcome_memory.py) fitted on the LAST 8 observed public events only - identically the recent8 baseline, exactly as in the graded guard.
fixed_parameters.action_scoring: Whichever model the decision rule selects, the choice is that model's RelationOutcomeMemory.choose output. An abstention is scored as a failed task, never as a success, and is reported separately.
fixed_parameters.archive_concordance_test: For each newest-window event e: the archive expectation is the reported outcome class (progress / damage / neutral) with the strictly highest count among ALL archive events whose span equals span(e) (same engineered span statistic); a tie for highest count, or an empty archive span set, gives expectation null. e is archive-MATCHED if its expectation is progress or damage AND e's own reported class is progress or damage. e is archive-CONCORDANT if it is archive-matched and its reported class EQUALS the expectation. concordant_count is the number of archive-concordant newest events (0..2); archive_matched_count is the number archive-matched (0..2). Raw integer counts only.
fixed_parameters.checkpoint: Append-only public events only; record/restore by canonical SHA256 replay exactly as the existing memory classes; restoring must reproduce the full decision record (immediate signal records, archive concordance records, counts, branch taken, acting source) and the choice identically. Maximum 1000 recorded events (existing MAX_SAMPLES).
fixed_parameters.decision_rule: Evaluated in this exact order on every decision once the signal is evaluable: (1) RECOVERY - if concordant_count == 2 AND opposed_count >= 1, act through the recovery model (source recorded as retained_archive). (2) ABSTENTION - else if opposed_count == 2, abstain (choose returns None), exactly the graded guard's protective response when a change is detected but no retained knowledge matches the newest evidence. (3) RECENT8 - otherwise act through the acting model exactly. There is no other input: no stage, phase, rule, or switch information, and no fitted probability enters any branch.
fixed_parameters.decision_rule_rationale: Recovery requires BOTH newest events concordant with the archive (a single concordant event is fully consistent with the known flip noise, exactly as a single opposed event was in the graded protocol) AND at least one of them opposed to the immediate reference (without any opposition there is no evidence of a return rather than a continuation, and the learner must behave as recent8/guard do - this clause is what keeps the recovery branch from silently replacing the acting model on stationary evidence wherever the archive happens to agree with it). Abstention retains priority over recent8 acting whenever a change is detected and recovery does not apply.
fixed_parameters.immediate_signal: IDENTICAL to the graded evidence-opposition guard, reused unchanged and not re-tuned: newest window = last 2 observed events; reference window = the 24 events immediately preceding the newest window (indices N-26 .. N-3). For each newest event, the reference expectation is the strictly-highest reported outcome class among reference events of equal span (tie or empty gives null); an event is matched if expectation and reported class are both progress or damage, and opposed if matched and different. opposed_count in 0..2. No fitted probabilities anywhere in either signal.
fixed_parameters.minimum_events_rule: Both signals together require a 2-event newest window, a full 24-event reference window, and at least 1 archive event: at least 27 observed events. Below 27 events neither signal is evaluable and the learner acts with a RelationOutcomeMemory fitted on all available events (recorded as not evaluable). Every benchmark checkpoint in this experiment has at least 240 observed events, so this fallback is never exercised during evaluation; it exists only so the class is well-defined for unit tests on short synthetic streams.
fixed_parameters.recovery_model: A RelationOutcomeMemory fitted on the retained archive events only (events[:N-26]), with the existing estimator and action scoring (utility 3 * p(progress) - 10 * p(damage), deterministic action-id tie break, via RelationOutcomeMemory.choose). The recovery model never includes the reference window or the newest window.
fixed_parameters.retained_archive: The retained archive is every observed event BEFORE the reference window: indices 0 .. N-27, i.e. events[:N-26]. It is not a snapshot, not phase-segmented, and receives no phase, stage, or switch information: at a return_A checkpoint it contains the full original-rule history plus the earlier part of the reversed-rule history, in chronological order, exactly as observed.
fixed_parameters.threshold_justification: Fixed a priori from the simulator's known noise rates and the graded guard's published aggregates, not from any score of this experiment (none exist). Per newest event at a return-A onset: archive matching is near-complete (the archive holds ~280 events at return-A checkpoints, ~28 per span band, so empty archive spans are rare and majorities are stable), and the archive majority is the original rule's class for every non-neutral span (original-rule events outnumber reversed-rule events in the archive roughly 240 to 40), so a newest event is archive-concordant with design probability approx 0.65-0.70 (non-neutral span fraction approx 0.8 x agreement with the true class approx 0.84 after the composed 0.1625 disagreement rate). Both events concordant: approx 0.42-0.49. opposed_count >= 1 at onset: approx 0.85 (guard's inspected onset mean opposed_count 1.0-1.06 of 2). Recovery therefore engages at a design approx 0.35-0.42 of return-A onset states, i.e. approx 2-2.5 of 6 states per cohort, each converting 16 episodes from abstention/stale acting to archive-model play at frozen_A's inspected per-state rate (68-70 successes per 6 states, approx 11 per state): expected candidate return-A pooled successes approx 25-35 against frozen_A's approx 68-70 - hence criterion 1's floor at 40 percent of frozen_A plus a guard-relative improvement floor, set BELOW the design expectation to allow binomial noise across only 6 states, and criterion 2's engagement floor at 2 of 6 states. At a B1 onset the archive majority is the original rule and the newest events reversed against it, so per-event concordance is only the flip-back probability approx 0.25-0.33 and both-concordant approx 0.06-0.11 of states - hence criterion 2's B1 ceiling of at most 1 of 6 states. Onset harm: recovery replaces abstention (0 harm, 0 successes) in its firing states with archive play at inspected archive/cumulative harm approx 4-8 per 16 episodes, and replaces stale recent8 play (inspected approx 13-16 harm per 16 episodes) in opposed_count == 1 states where recovery engages; false recovery at B1 (design approx 0.06-0.11 of states, harm approx 16 in such a state) is the offsetting cost - net pooled onset harm is expected at or below the guard's, which is exactly criterion 3's falsifiable bound.

candidate.name: EvidenceOppositionRecoveryMemory
candidate.placement: New separate optional learner class in developmental_ai/. The default controller and every existing learner are untouched; existing learners appear only as baselines. The graded EvidenceOppositionGuardMemory is a baseline in this experiment, not modified by it.

capability_under_test: Detection WITH recovery at a return to a previously learned rule: whether a learner that pairs the graded evidence-opposition onset signal (computed from the observed evidence itself, no fitted probabilities) with a retained-knowledge concordance test can, at return_A checkpoints 2 and 4, act through retained pre-switch knowledge instead of merely abstaining or acting through a stale recent window - approaching frozen_A's return-A successes while keeping pooled onset harm at or below the evidence-opposition guard's level on the same cohort. Priority 1 items 2 + 3 joined to item 4 (strengthen long-term retention; prevent new learning from overwriting established knowledge; improve adaptation to changing environments); handoff section 8 slow or incorrect recovery of old knowledge and first-contact overconfidence.

checkpoints.note: A checkpoint value k means the learner has observed the full A history plus the first k TRAIN events of the named stage (control: first k continuation events). Checkpoints 2 and 4 are the graded recovery window for return_A and the graded onset window for harm; 8 and 16 report persistence costs; 32 grades release. return_A has 48 TRAIN events and the control continuation 64, so 32 is within range for every arm. Checkpoint 0 is a reported diagnostic, NOT graded: at k=0 the stream contains zero post-switch events, so no evidence-driven learner can distinguish the switched world from the pre-switch world (and by the decision rule recovery cannot engage at k=0 of B1/B2, where opposed_count is 0 on pre-switch evidence).

cohorts.novelty_statement: Both cohorts are NEW and uninspected as of this freeze. They are disjoint from every cohort in the inspected records, including 17/23/41, 1009/1013/1031, 2749/6607/9901, 14003/14009/14033, 15101/22003/31013, 17431/24869/37021, 27007/27011/27017, 43103/50021/61031, 72019/83003/94009, the earlier experiments' 292003/292021/292039 and 293001/293017/293041, the preceding experiments' 302003/302021/302039, 303001/303017/303041, 312003/312021/312039, and 313001/313017/313041. Disjointness was verified by searching all files under projects/developmental-ai/ for the six seed values before this commit; none occurred. Both cohorts become INSPECTED once evaluated under this protocol.

grading.ci_claims: Linux/Windows validation is claimed only for an exact commit with a real GitHub Actions run on that commit; otherwise it is recorded as UNVERIFIED.
grading.cumulative_cap: If the cumulative baseline's pooled return-A onset successes exceed the candidate's by more than 8 on BOTH cohorts, the conclusion is capped at Partially demonstrated regardless of criterion outcomes: plain cumulative retention would then dominate the candidate's signal-gated recovery, and the honest finding is that retention was already available without the mechanism under test.
grading.demonstrated: All seven criteria PASS on BOTH cohorts, the historical transfer benchmark (benchmarks.transfer_benchmark, unchanged) still passes, and the full unit suite (python -m unittest discover -s tests) passes on the evaluation commit - subject to the cumulative cap below.
grading.failed: Any of criteria 1-4 FAILs on the additional cohort, or criterion 7 FAILs on either cohort.
grading.format: Handoff section 6 report format. Every acceptance criterion above is graded PASS or FAIL individually, per cohort; no failed criterion may be hidden inside an overall positive summary.
grading.generalization_level: At most handoff level 2-3 (choosing among / applying already-supplied representations under a rule change, plus designer-supplied signal, concordance, and routing rules). No level-6 or novel-representation claim is permitted from this experiment: the A/B rules, span statistic, windows, archive definition, and decision rule are all designer-supplied. A PASS would demonstrate signal-gated recovery of retained knowledge at a first return in this simulator only, not general regime identification (the archive is global and unsegmented; B2 recovery is pre-registered as not expected), not calibrated uncertainty, and not real-world safety.
grading.partially_demonstrated: Criteria 1, 3, and 7 PASS on both cohorts but criterion 2, 4, 5, or 6 FAILs on either cohort, or all criteria PASS on the development cohort only, or the cumulative cap applies.
grading.regression: The candidate's pooled onset harm exceeds recent8's on both cohorts, or the candidate's stationary-control successes fall below recent8's by more than 6 on both cohorts, or the historical transfer benchmark or full unit suite breaks.

hypothesis: At a return_A onset the newest events disagree with the immediately preceding (reversed-rule) evidence but AGREE with the much older retained evidence, because the original rule dominated the stream for 240 events before any switch. That asymmetry is measurable with the same raw-count machinery as the graded guard, pointed at a different window: a hard span-majority expectation built from ALL retained events before the 24-event reference window (the archive) will be matched and concordant for both newest events at a substantial minority of return-A onset states (design approx 0.4 of states), will almost never be concordant for both newest events at a B1 onset (no reversed-rule knowledge is retained yet, and the archive majority is the original rule the newest events reversed against), and acting through a relation model fitted on that archive in exactly the concordant-and-opposed states converts the guard's abstentions and part of its stale recent8 acting into frozen_A-like successes at frozen_A-like harm, without raising pooled onset harm above the guard's level.
limitation_evidence: EVIDENCE_OPPOSITION_ONSET_GUARD (docs/EVIDENCE_OPPOSITION_ONSET_GUARD.md, graded Demonstrated 2026-10-29, cohorts 312003-family / 313001-family now INSPECTED): all six criteria PASS on both cohorts, but at return_A checkpoints 2 and 4 pooled the candidate scored 10 (development) / 4 (additional) successes against frozen_A's 68 / 70 on the same cells, while cumulative - a plain relation model on all observed events - scored 64 / 64. The guard abstains when its gate fires (return-A gate fired in 2 of 6 seed-checkpoint states per cohort, each abstaining 16 of 16 episodes) and acts through stale recent8 when it does not (opposed_count 1 in 3 of 6 development and 4 of 6 additional return-A states). Detection exists; recovery does not.

Same experiment, return-A onset harm on inspected cohorts: candidate 54 / 60 pooled harmful TEST actions at checkpoints 2 and 4 versus recent8 80 / 86 and frozen_A 28 / 26 - abstention avoided the firing states' harm (0 there) but the non-firing states reproduced recent8's stale-model harm almost in full.

EARLY_POST_SWITCH_ADAPTATION (graded Failed / Regression 2026-10-28): an archive-routing candidate DID recover partially at return-A-8 (29 successes development, matching frozen_A's 29) but its contradiction override routed through recent32, still stale at onset checkpoints, and it regressed elsewhere. Archive routing is not new; routing at FIRST CONTACT (k=2,4), triggered by an evidence-count signal and gated by a concordance test against the newest evidence itself, is what has not been tried.
Handoff section 8 standing limitations: slow or incorrect recovery of old knowledge remains a listed persistent weakness.
metrics_reported: Per seed, per stage (B1, return_A, B2, control), per checkpoint, per method: successes, harmful TEST actions, failed-by-abstention count, attempted tasks.

Candidate decision record at every checkpoint, per seed: the immediate signal record exactly as in the graded guard protocol (per newest-window event: span, reported outcome class, reference event count, reference majority class or null, matched flag, opposed flag; plus opposed_count, matched_count), the archive concordance record (per newest-window event: span, reported outcome class, archive event count for that span, archive majority class or null, archive-matched flag, archive-concordant flag; plus concordant_count, archive_matched_count), the branch taken (retained_archive / abstained / recent8 / all_available_below_minimum), recovery-fired flag, abstained flag, gate-evaluable flag, and the acting source.

Recovery engagement aggregates per cohort, from the decision records alone: recovery-fired states, abstention states, and recent8 states among the 6 return-A onset states, the 6 B1 onset states, the 6 B2 onset states, and the graded control states.
Onset harm and successes at checkpoint 0 for every stage, per seed and method, reported explicitly as a diagnostic and never pooled into any graded onset figure and never hidden.
Persistence cost: candidate abstentions, recovery engagements, successes, and harm at checkpoints 8 and 16 per stage, reported alongside the checkpoint-32 release figures.
Per seed TRAIN accounting, counted once regardless of checkpoints or methods: actor actions, actual harmful actions, actual productive, actual neutral, reported harmful, report label flips.
Learner-issued information-acquisition actions (frozen at 0) and any additional observations requested (frozen at 0).
Checkpoint record SHA256 and restore-replay identity for the candidate.
No pooled-only reporting: every cohort figure must be decomposable into its three per-seed rows, and every pooled criterion figure into its per-cell rows.
permitted_observations: The learner sees only the public reported stream of {features, progress, damage} events in chronological order, identical for every method, plus the public TEST frame (actions with public features) at decision time. No phase label, rule identity, episode index, true (unflipped) outcome, report-flip flag, simulator state, or TEST outcome may enter the learner, its signals, its recovery model, or its checkpoint record.
priority: MUSE_BUILD_ORDER Priority 1 (Independent Learning), items 2, 3, and 4. This experiment deliberately builds on the one Demonstrated result of the campaign so far: the evidence-count onset signal exists and is selective; what is missing is any response to it other than abstention at the one stage (return_A) where retained knowledge is immediately usable.
registration: This protocol is committed BEFORE any candidate implementation, unit test, benchmark harness, or score inspection for this experiment. Once either cohort is evaluated, its seeds are INSPECTED: no parameter, threshold, seed, checkpoint, or acceptance criterion in this file may be revised against those results. A revised hypothesis requires a NEW protocol file and NEW seed cohorts. No parameter of the three graded onset experiments (early_post_switch_adaptation, first_contact_onset_guard, evidence_opposition_onset_guard) was re-tuned against its inspected cohorts in designing this protocol: the immediate opposition signal below is reused EXACTLY as frozen in the evidence-opposition protocol (newest window 2, reference window 24, opposed_count definition unchanged), and the new elements - the retained-archive concordance test, the recovery decision order, and every threshold - are derived a priori from the graded guard's published diagnosis and the simulator's known noise rates (1/8 stochastic flips, 1/20 report flips), as derived in candidate.fixed_parameters.threshold_justification.
required_evaluation_runs: This experiment's frozen benchmark on the development cohort and on the additional cohort, exactly as registered here.
Full unit suite: python -m unittest discover -s tests

simulator.actor: Independent hash-seeded random first-action actor, one action per disposable TRAIN episode, identical stream for every method. The learner issues ZERO training interventions of its own (acquisition budget = 0; see budgets).
simulator.family: StochasticWorld exactly as implemented in benchmarks/stochastic_prequential_benchmark.py (SameSchemaWorld two public numeric features inlet/outlet, anonymous actions, authored span-to-effect bands). No simulator code is changed by this experiment; the benchmark harness for this experiment reuses StochasticWorld and public_train unchanged.
simulator.hidden_rules: Hidden physics schedule per seed: A (original progress/damage mapping) -> B1 (progress/damage inverted) -> return_A (original) -> B2 (inverted). Phase boundaries, phase names, and the active rule are benchmark-private and are never supplied to any learner.
simulator.reported_feedback: An independent sha256 draw on (seed, TRAIN episode index) flips a non-neutral TRAIN reported progress/damage label with probability 1/20, exactly as in public_train. The learner receives only the possibly corrupted public report. Actual actor harm and label flips are counted separately by the benchmark.
simulator.stationary_control_arm: A separate arm per seed with NO rule change: 240 A TRAIN episodes (indices 1000..1239) followed by 64 further A TRAIN episodes (indices 5000..5063, physics original). It measures recovery-branch selectivity: false engagement, false abstention, and lost productivity when nothing changed.
simulator.true_stochastic_feedback: Every actual non-neutral simulator action has probability 1/8 of a progress/damage flip, drawn by deterministic sha256 of (seed, split, episode index, action id, tick) exactly as in StochasticWorld._sample_outcome. Neutral outcomes stay neutral. TEST outcomes are the realized stochastic outcomes, not clean deterministic ones.

test.repeated_indices_note: The same TEST indices are re-scored at every checkpoint by every method; checkpoint rows are therefore not independent samples. TEST is read-only: no TEST outcome is ever trained on, and the harness must verify each method's checkpoint record is unchanged after TEST evaluation (contamination check, as in stochastic_prequential_benchmark).

training_indices.control_A_continuation: 5000..5063 (64 episodes, physics original, stationary control arm only)
